players.product: solid-state transformer (13.8-34.5 kV to 800-1500 VDC) and solid-state circuit breakers for 800 VDC AI data centers (in development, Infineon SiC inside)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results: GAAP revenue $346.2 million, up 11.5% quarter-over-quarter and 19.6% year-over-year; non-GAAP revenue $345.5 million, up 23% year-over-year, above the midpoint of guidance, with no significant pull forward of revenue from safe harbor. By region: U.S. $154.9 million (down 2% q/q, 44.7% of revenue), Europe $154.4 million (up 36% q/q, 44.6%), international $36.9 million (down 5% q/q, 10.7%). CEO Shuki Nir: European revenue more than doubled year-over-year.
quarterly_data.figure: GAAP revenue $346.2 million (+19.6% y/y); non-GAAP revenue $345.5 million (+23% y/y); U.S. $154.9 million, Europe $154.4 million, international $36.9 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 margins and profitability: GAAP gross margin 27.5% (22% in Q1, 11.1% a year earlier); non-GAAP gross margin 28.6% (23.5%, 13.1%), above the high end of guidance, including a $13.3 million gross benefit from IEEPA tariff refunds. Non-GAAP operating income $10.2 million on non-GAAP opex of $88.5 million - the first non-GAAP operating profitability in nearly three years (CEO); GAAP operating loss $16 million; GAAP net loss $30.8 million; non-GAAP net income $3.6 million, positive for the first time since Q2 2023. Cash, equivalents and marketable securities $601.6 million at June 30, 2026 (vs $581.1 million at December 31, 2025); Q2 free cash flow $3.1 million.
quarterly_data.figure: GAAP gross margin 27.5%; non-GAAP gross margin 28.6% (incl. $13.3 million IEEPA refunds); non-GAAP operating income $10.2 million; GAAP net loss $30.8 million; cash and securities $601.6 million

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: revenue $310 million-$340 million, with most of the sequential decline in Europe (approximately $15 million at the midpoint, mainly seasonality) and no typical third-quarter pickup expected in the U.S. given continued market softness; non-GAAP gross margin approximately 22%-26% (excluding potential IEEPA refunds); non-GAAP opex approximately $86 million-$91 million. CFO Maoz Sigron: including the $11.5 million of IEEPA refunds already received in July, the guidance midpoint implies a non-GAAP operating profit in Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $310 million-$340 million; non-GAAP gross margin 22%-26%; non-GAAP opex $86 million-$91 million; $11.5 million IEEPA refunds received in July

quarterly_data.signal: Capex: $12 million in the first half; full-year 2026 capex still expected at $60 million-$80 million, for increased U.S. production capacity for PV and batteries, the new headquarters in Israel (largely advanced R&D facilities), investment related to the AI factory offering, and maintenance. CFO: continues to expect positive free cash flow for the full year, including the ongoing ability to monetize 45X credits.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 capex $12 million; 2026 capex $60 million-$80 million

quarterly_data.signal: AI factory solid-state transformer (SST): CEO Shuki Nir said the data center business shifted from development to demonstration in Q2 - prospective customers, including their technical and engineering teams, saw live demonstrations of the SST in SolarEdge's labs, which validated 99% efficiency across a range of power levels, direct conversion from medium voltage AC to a regulated DC bus, and encouraging installation results. CFO: the company demonstrated a working prototype going from medium voltage to 800 V DC regulated. Efficiency is a key focus in the RFIs it has responded to.

SST roadmap: CEO - next milestones are a working system in the lab by the end of 2026, pilot installations in 2027 and volume shipments in 2028; CFO - the proof-of-concept prototype is to be fully working at the full three-phase 34.5 kV voltage by year end, with 2027 pilots at data centers so that there could be meaningful revenue in 2028. CEO: expects SST revenue to start in 2028, describing NVIDIA sharing its 800 V GPU roadmap with the ecosystem as step one and the move from sidecar or other inefficient solutions to SSTs as step two; more detail promised at the September 10 Investor Day.
quarterly_data.figure: lab working system end of 2026; pilots 2027; volume shipments 2028; 34.5 kV prototype

quarterly_data.signal: U.S. commercial & industrial (C&I): CEO - SolarEdge's share rose to more than 50% of U.S. C&I rooftop installations in the most recent report, and its systems are installed on rooftops of more than 60% of Fortune 100 companies; he says it has been the only major C&I inverter vendor to deliver U.S.-manufactured products at scale meeting domestic content, non-FEOC and FCC Covered List requirements, with most manufacturing in Utah, Florida and Texas. CEO: of the three C&I leaders (SMA, Chint and SolarEdge), the other two, to the best of his knowledge, do not comply with both FEOC and domestic content; he expects the C&I outlook to stay positive on rising electricity prices and data center-driven demand.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 50% of U.S. C&I rooftop installations; more than 60% of Fortune 100 companies

quarterly_data.signal: U.S. residential: CEO - demand remained soft in Q2 as customers navigated a slower tax equity funding environment and uncertainty around FEOC, straining installers and leading distributors to cut purchases and inventory; he expects the softness to continue in Q3, says channel inventory is normalized, and expects SolarEdge to gain share when the market rebounds given its fit with the TPO model. SolarEdge signed a significant amount of safe harbor transactions in both resi and C&I ahead of the July 4 deadline, under the physical work test (revenue aligned with customers' installations).

Nexis platform: three-phase Nexis began a meaningful rollout in Europe in Q2 with shipments exceeding $60 million; single-phase Nexis rollout in Europe planned for Q1 2027; U.S. rollout starting in Q3 2026, approved on a growing list of U.S. financing platforms (TPO, prepaid PPA and loan). Retrofit campaigns in the Netherlands and DACH (combined installed base greater than 1 million homes) generated more than $20 million of upsell in Q2. CEO: Nexis is made in the U.S. by a U.S. company and needs no FCC exemption; storage prices remained stable per product and storage is expected to become a bigger piece of the business.
quarterly_data.figure: Nexis shipments exceeding $60 million in Q2; more than $20 million upsell; installed base greater than 1 million homes

quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain: CEO - data center demand is creating strain on some components, memory in particular; SolarEdge has had to absorb some memory price increases, which he called not significant in the grand scheme, while its supply chain team works with partners to secure supply.
